title: Whoever It Is, Whatever It Is

sections.title: What you know
sections.content: You know *pase lo que pase* and *diga lo que diga* from B2 Unit 8, and the others like them (*venga quien venga*, *estés donde estés*). The verb is said twice, around a relative word, to say that it makes no difference. This lesson adds three frames with *ser* that match the relatives of this unit.

sections.title: The repeated verb with ser
rows: Sea quien sea, no le abras la puerta.
Whoever it is, don't open the door to them. (Like *quienquiera que sea*.)
Sea cual sea tu respuesta, la voy a respetar.
Whatever your answer is, I'll respect it. (Like *cualquiera que sea*.)
Sean cuales sean las razones, la decisión es tuya.
Whatever the reasons are, the decision is yours.

sections.title: Singular and plural
sections.content: *Sea cual sea* agrees with the thing you are talking about: *sea cual sea la razón*, *sean cuales sean las razones*. With a different verb the pattern is the one you know: *Llame quien llame, no abras la puerta*. The repeated form is short and firm, so you hear it a lot in speech; *cualquiera que sea* is longer and more common in writing.

items.spanish: Llame quien llame, no abras la puerta.
items.english: Whoever calls, don't open the door.

items.spanish: Sea cual sea el resultado, vamos a aceptarlo.
items.english: Whatever the result is, we're going to accept it.

items.spanish: Opinen lo que opinen, tú decides.
Vaya donde vaya, siempre llama a su madre.
items.english: Wherever she goes, she always calls her mother.

sections.content: The two verbs must match: *sea cual sea*, never *sea cual es*. In *sea cual sea* the first *sea* is the subjunctive of *ser*, and it must agree with the noun: *sean cuales sean* for a plural.
